result.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
result.summary: Modern language models undergo reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on top of already-trained checkpoints. A key promise of RLVR is the discovery of new reasoning strategies. In principle, a model can sample novel ideas absent from its prior training data. In practice, however, augmenting RLVR with strong novelty incentives has seen limited success and can degrade model quality. Because verifiable rewards supervise only a narrow slice of the model's knowledge and behavior, such degradations are difficult to recover from. Instead, we decouple exploration from optimization in a framework we call Exploration-Distillation (ExpDis). We train one or more explorer policies with a novelty bonus in the reward, filter their trajectories for correctness and quality, and distill them into a separate student policy. The student policy is then trained without a novelty bonus. We repeat the above procedure for several rounds, alternating between exploration and optimization. This decoupling allows us to aggressively scale exploration without degrading the student policy. Across seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two model families, ExpDis outperforms DAPO at the same wall-clock budget. Moreover, we observe improved pass@$k$ scaling, indicating that ExpDis produces models that generate more diverse correct solutions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Exploration-Distillation（ExpDis），在 RLVR 中把带新颖性奖励的探索策略与不带新颖性奖励的学生策略解耦，通过多轮「探索—筛选正确优质轨迹—蒸馏」循环训练，在数学推理基准上提升 pass@k 多样性。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 RLVR 工作，但其「探索策略生成多样轨迹、经正确性与质量筛选后蒸馏到学生策略」的分离式监督流程，可能为 LVR 的轨迹训练、视觉证据筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索。
